YOUR CIRCLE. YOUR CHALLENGE.

Choose your start.

You pick the center. We choose the most varied valid starting circle and deal six different hand digits. Place tiles one after another to grow the board.

Center digit

Score = tiles you place. The starting seven don’t count. Hints and hand swaps cost 10 seconds in timed rounds. The clock starts when you press the button below.

A LITTLE MATH GOES A LONG WAY.

Time’s up.

0HEXES PLACED

SIX IN YOUR HAND. ROOM TO GROW.

Make every triangle count.

  1. Four hexes make a side.

    A side looks like 1–4–7–1. Add its two interior digits: 4 + 7 = 11. The last digit is 1, so both ends are 1. Another valid side is 5–1–4–5.

  2. All three corners match.

    The board outlines larger triangles with four hexes per side. All three corners of each outlined triangle must carry the same digit, and each side’s two interior numbers must add to that digit. New triangles are tracked as sides take shape.

  3. Keep placing tiles.

    Choose a hand tile and an outlined empty hex. Extend two consecutive numbers along a straight line, or fill a missing position on a tracked side. Every placement must agree with all the larger triangles it touches. You can build around the board, not only at the last tile.

  4. One placed. One drawn. Play again.

    Every valid tile scores one hex and draws one replacement into your six-tile hand. Keep going until a round limit is reached or no legal space remains. A wrong digit uses a mistake without consuming a tile. Hints and hand swaps cost 10 seconds in timed rounds.
